basics.name: Jai N. Veilleux
basics.label: M.S. student in Quantum Information Science
basics.summary: Research interests include open quantum systems, quantum error correction, and scientific computing.

projects.name: Temporal calibration for a Steane memory
projects.summary: Wrote the Qiskit implementation for Team Bells Pair at Qompute 2026. Simulated repeated correction in a seven-qubit Steane memory, implemented independent calibration circuits, and compared four decoders on held-out records.

projects.name: Spectator-qubit dynamics on IBM Fez
projects.summary: Extended a USC course project into a three-job IBM Fez experiment. Reconstructed a central qubit's state and measured a trace-distance revival under coherent exchange and a decrease in the spectator-reset control.

projects.name: Qiskit circuit library and transpiler
projects.summary: Proposed a Rust qDRIFT implementation for the C API and collaborated on its follow-up. Submitted separate changes for delay padding, classical type logic, and Windows library discovery.

projects.name: Gate-model QAOA for binary image denoising
projects.summary: USC graduate course project. Mapped a restricted Boltzmann machine denoising objective to an Ising Hamiltonian and compared exact optimization, Aer simulation, and IBM hardware.

projects.name: SamplableSet for Rust
projects.summary: Ported a weighted-sampling data structure from C++ to Rust. Used composition-rejection sampling with dynamically updated weights.

projects.name: qpgf
projects.summary: UVM course prototype for exploring distributions of assumed gate-error counts with probability generating functions and calibration-derived inputs.

projects.name: Independent study in quantum computation
projects.summary: Implemented quantum circuit Born machines and a quantum Hamiltonian-based model and presented the project at the December 2024 UVM CS Fair.

projects.name: Optical demonstration of BB84
projects.summary: Built an Arduino-controlled optical link with software-simulated polarization choices. Presented the project at the Edmonds College Undergraduate Research Symposium.

work.name: The University of Vermont
work.position: Teaching Assistant (grader), Algorithm Design and Analysis
work.summary: Graded programming and written assignments, answered student questions, and flagged assignment issues for course staff.

work.name: Airship AI
work.summary: Diagnosed Windows Server issues, automated repetitive support tasks, and set up a Git server for team scripts. Wrote troubleshooting documentation for customers and contractors.

work.name: The IT Support Center, LLC.
work.summary: Troubleshot IT issues for customers remotely and documented solutions.
